two_findings: StreamRunIndex samples and dirCum are global quantities, so the carry must include occ/cum/lastSample/lastSampleOcc/index-row - not just the open run and the sweep state.

write() patches each char's last sample with the distance to the end of the observed stream, so a mid-stream group writes a wrong tail stride; the merged m13 needs a carried per-char repair (<=256 entries), which is why the merged member is byte-identical rather than 'self-consistent'.
A group cut must land on a global run index divisible by M1_BLOCK_RUNS=1024 (m1 blocks carry their own padded bit streams); this is a numbered refusal, not a comment.
correction: the 'first frame byte equals the carried code' guard I asked for is wrong at a run boundary - the byte changes there by definition. The writer asserts the two legal continuations instead: same code grows the carried run by one row ending at this position, different code starts a fresh one-row run.
